content.text:
I couldn't run the maintenance. Every snapshot expiry call came back with "tool call limit reached; not run," so nothing was changed. No snapshots were expired, no orphan files were deleted, and all tables are as they were. I didn't get to the orphan file cleanup.

**What I found first:** there are 7 tables, and most of them keep a long snapshot history:

| Table | Snapshots | Current snapshot (committed) |
|---|---|---|
| db.customers | 3 | 100013 (2026-10-23) |
| db.customers_pii | 2 | 100015 (2026-10-23) |
| db.events | 6 | 100021 (2026-11-02) |
| db.orders | 8 | 100008 (2026-11-03) |
| db.orders_staging | 2 | 100010 (2026-11-02) |
| prod.customers | 1 | 100025 (2026-09-05) |
| prod.orders | 3 | 100024 (2026-11-02) |

**What I'd planned to run:** expire everything older than 2026-11-04T00:00Z on each table, always keeping the current snapshot, then remove orphan files.

**Before you retry, two things to know:**
- **This can't be undone.** Once the old snapshots are gone, you can't roll back or look at earlier versions of any table, including the two production ones (`prod.orders` and `prod.customers`).
- **Deleting orphan files up to "right now" can break writes that are still running.** A job that's still writing has files no snapshot points to yet, and they'd be deleted. That's why this cleanup normally only touches files older than about 3 days. I'd suggest that cutoff, e.g. `older_than` = 2026-11-01, unless you're sure nothing is writing.

Once the tool limit resets, I can run it again as you asked or with the safer orphan cutoff.
